situation:
You are the store operations coordinator at NORTHBANK COFFEE, a chain of thirty-six shops formed six months ago when Northbank bought KETTLE ROW COFFEE. The district manager (judge) has asked you to recommend what daily information the company should put in front of its shift leads.

The two chains still run separate registers. Northbank shops see sales by the hour on a screen; former Kettle Row shops get a printed sheet the next morning, and the numbers on it are not counted the same way. The district manager (judge) cannot compare one shop to another without rebuilding both by hand.

One system would fix that. Putting every shop on the same registers and the same fixed price list would give the company one comparable set of numbers each day. It would also end what customers name when asked why they come: each manager prices a few local items and rotates a small menu on what that shift sees selling.

The company could instead leave local pricing alone and have shift leads fill in one shared sheet by hand, which keeps the district waiting a day and keeps two sets of numbers that do not line up. The district manager (judge) wants your recommendation and the reasoning behind it.

You will present it in the district office. The district manager (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the questions, the district manager (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are to assume the role of district manager of NORTHBANK COFFEE, a chain of thirty-six shops formed six months ago when Northbank bought KETTLE ROW COFFEE.

Business background is the same as the situation above. The two chains still run separate registers whose numbers are not counted the same way, one system with one fixed price list would make the shops comparable, and the local pricing and rotating menu the managers set are what customers name when they are asked why they come.

You have asked the store operations coordinator (participant) to recommend what daily information the company should put in front of its shift leads, and to give you the reasoning behind that recommendation.

During the course of the role-play you are to ask the participant the following questions:
judgeQuestions: What does the choice you set aside give up?
